Decision series was just the beginning of modern mobile gaming. I played the first and second Decision in my childhood, and I liked the game very much, especially the second one, but as I replayed the whole series after this many years, I could tell the many flaws and even its eventual downfall of the Decision series. Let's start from the good parts. The game has multiple weapons, skills, and regional upgrades for the player to unlock. Most weapons have their respective usage on different scenarios, and the pace of progression is just well enough for the player to discover and try out new things. I speak on behalf of the first two games. The medieval-themed and the third installment exposed the game's critical flaw: that Decision series' gameplay loop design was addicting and not inherently fun. In the game, every thing you want to unlock requires a certain level of grinding for resources. On its core, it is simply the "number goes bigger" types of game. Nothing really change for the gameplay itself as literally everything you want in this series requires you to mindlessly kill zombies, with slightly better weapons and skills over time, but nothing really changes. Enemy types are very limited and you would soon discover that other than a gradual growth in numbers, there is nothing challenging or interesting. Stripping away the part where you have to do a "defense mission" for every single construction and recruitment, the gameplay is just mobile gaming that could have very much added an "auto-fight" or "fight-skip" feature. Upgrading and exploring more areas give you bigger number of enemies, damage output, and passive income, while you are doing essentially the same thing over and over. This is just addictive mobile trash gaming disguised as video game. Hack, I haven't even talked about the worst parts. To slow down your progress, every installment would have an occasional "zombie outbreak" event where you have to play a tower defense mission to prevent zombies from overtaking your region. The defense missions are extremely tedious and they require no skill whatsoever. You simply control a machine-gun tower and strife the enemies down with little to no risk involved since the enemies can't reach you. It is just a chore that the game forces you to do every once in a while. The medieval-themed is the beginning of a downfall. The close combat gameplay is just holding down the mouse and fight enemies walking in a circle. There are some cool skills to unlock but it does not help. Ironically enough, the best weapon is still ranged ones. Who could have guessed that in a world where the majority of enemies wield melee weapons, ranged weapons becomes the best weapon of choice? I bought the first bow appearing in the game and used that bow to the end of the game, saving me tons of time and money buying other decorative melee-related skills and weapons. I can't say much about Decision 3 because the game has depleted my patience after the end of the medieval one. It is literally the same thing but more tedious. Recon an area, build constructions, buy better weapons and skills, build more constructions, recon the next area...rinse and repeat, except now they added mandatory AI as a new requirement. The AI is so dumb and slow that I believe the only thing it adds to the game is to lengthen your playtime. If you want to check this game out for yourself, just play Decision 2 and skip the rest.

Decision Legacy Collection is an ancient collection of Flash games from 2012. It's a whopping 14 years old at the time of this review. The games lack support for the typical features of modern gaming PCs, and haven't been modernised or updated to run smoothly on contemporary machines. The collection looks and feels dated. Despite this lack of modernisation, it carries a pretty high price tag for such old games. This seems to have be lingering on Steam with an inflated price to try profit from abandonware. The games themselves are really badly made top down twin stick shooters where you just shoot waves of zombies... it's a snorefest that would only appeal to kids who could only afford to play crap browser/Flash games. So yeah. Ten bucks on Steam for free browser games. Valve has no ethics filter on Steam Direct. From a technical perspective, the collection doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard. A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics. It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the games is extremely low as a result. The graphics aren't great. ancient Adobe Flash pixelcrap That will understandably a turn off for a lot of gamers, and it's a big contributor to the failure of the games to attract gamers despite having no up-front cost. Gaming is a primarily visual medium, and if developers want to succeed, they must understand that it's not an area for compromise. You deserve better than compromises. There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks. There's no way to ensure these are running at the native resolution of your display. There's no guarantee these games will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision. The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the games unplayable for differently-abled gamers, left handed gamers or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts. Let's cut to the core problem here. This is a collection of Adobe Flash/AIR games. It's now 2026, and these were released back in 2012, gamers and the industry expect and deserve better than this kind of low effort shovelware. These were designed to run in a web browser. They have no place in your Steam library, which is for PC games. It's impossible for Adobe Flash games made for web browsers to compare even remotely well to professionally developed PC games. These technical defects push this collection below acceptable standards for any modern PC game. So, should you buy these games? Is this collection one of the best of the 130,000+ games on Steam? Decision Legacy Collection is relatively expensive for an abandonware nostalgia gouge, at $10 USD, and it's not worth it. The games are just too old, haven't been modernised. And as the old saying goes, you can't go home again. For comparison, the $10 asking price for this collection could get you games like "The Vanishing of Ethan Carter", "Ghostrunner" or "Rise of the Tomb Raider". No pixelcrap is worth $10. If developers want to get paid the same kind of money as real game developers who know how to do graphics properly, they need to learn how to do graphics properly. We must also question the ethics of a game publisher charging TEN BUCKS FOR FREE BROWSER GAMES. This is a serial pattern of highly unethical behaviour from this "publisher"... trying to scam gamers into paying cash money for free browser games is reprehensible.

A collection of flash era games; this one in especific was one of my favorites. Decision I sets the scene: You made the decision to help humanity fight back against the waves of undead, and to do so you must Recon, Clear and Rebuild the Tower and Factory in each sector back to a sustainable territory, making it a safe haven. You need to kill to earn money to spend on the areas or on yourself and your weapons; couldn't get any more simpler. Decision II gives you a whole new city to reconquer and the EXP bars for each weapon, encouraging you to use each until they max out; however, this time you'll be going against tougher and bigger enemies, including some mutants and trolls, be it on the areas or Outside (endless mode for farming EXP or money). Also, collectibles like ATMs and Stashes are not shown on the radar yet. Decision Medieval switches the gun n' run to a melee focused combat; they give you way too many blades to level up, so a inventory system was a great addition. The skills also gave a lot more ways to fight, like charming an enemy to your team or making it go berserk; not only that, the collectibles are now visible on eagle vision (which is a relief). Only problem people have with this one is the grind, since on endgame you'll be rich of crates (resources) and money poor, forcing you to go outside A LOT. Also, Orcs are present, and they hate the zombies, so it's now a three sided war. Decision III went bold and decided to add the NPC system, in which you need to find and recruit certain people you find to get them to help you rebuild, like getting a soldier to man the turret or a builder to repair the factory; this addition is amazing on paper and it really is until the midgame, but as endgame arrives the game forces you to WANDER EVERYWHERE to find that single Engineer you need for the final upgrade on your last factory (this could have been fixed with an upgrade that could make NPCs switch jobs, like a School). Also, one thing I've seen on this one is that some maps and enemies are just reskins of things you could find in Medieval (Mutants are just reskined Orcs, even the trolls). Altough we do have some bugs and perfomance issues, this is still a great game from 2010-2014, and I'm happy that I could not only replay them but also 100% them. Now, for the achievements: In short, play all of them and finish all of their in-game achievements, with a few caveats: Decision I: you have 40 days to recon all areas and find three dead soldiers, so rush tower and do tower assaults and DO NOT MAX OUT AREAS EARLY, since you do not have the option to wander yet. Also, when maxing out areas, remember to build ALL of the tower types, since you need to kill a bunch with each type. Decision II: way easier, just remember to rush Detector and Hacker III. Decision Medieval: rush Eagle Vision and Picklock III, and prepare for a lot of grinding. Try to let them capture your territory, since every recon tends to net you 10k. Decision III: rush Detector III and Hacker III for profit, send everyone to base except a few soldiers, civilians and engineers (the last two are VERY important and give you money each day, and the soldier is used to upgrade the tower), and also keep a builder/ranger on team to farm materials. Don't worry on losing territory, each recon tends to net around 10k. Other than that, here's what you should know about the jobs: * Soldier: save them for tower and shelter upgrades; * Captain: use them damage/money upgrades and for your team later (RPGs); * Ranger: save them for Decoy upgrades and for your team later (MINIGUNS); * Engineer: SAVE THEM, you need 3 to max out each factory and a few for the wall upgrades for a single tower; * Builder: save one for each factory and the wall upgrades, then use the rest to upgrade the factory performance; * Citizen: save one for each Team Size upgrade, then keep the rest in your team to help you with upkeep costs and net you a nice sum each day.
Just as Good as I remember. Highly Recommend.

I'm on the fence between positive and negative. On one hand, it's a collection of good old classic games from a flash era. They are still enjoyable and playable today, if not a little grindy. But I have to lean towards a negative review, because of 2 main issues: 1. The game is buggy. Very buggy. If you're an achievement completionist, expect grind - but a 1 small bug can softlock you from getting one of the achievements, and you have to start all over, nullifying 10+ hours of your progress. That's exactly what happened to me and it's infuriating. 2. The performance has no business being that bad. I'm running this game on a high end PC, and not only the FPS are hard limited (understandable), but more importantly the game feels unreponsive and laggy (not understandable). I felt like it played better way back, via a browser, and for free. I really want to support the developers, but they're not making it easy.

Hello team members of FlyAnvil, I am a Chinese player, currently 22 years old and a university student. When I was about 8 years old, I played Decision 1 – although it was a pirated copy, your Decision 1 really captured my attention. In the following years, I also played Decision 2, Decision 3, the Medieval version, and the newly released Blood Haze – I love them all. This series has grown up with me. I always enjoyed exploring new strategies and bugs in Decision 3, completely absorbed in it. Starting from 2014, I've been deeply hooked on Decision 3 to this day. At first I played it on pirate websites, but around 2020 I gradually found my way to the Armor Games website, and I even earned all achievements for Decisions 1-3 and the Medieval version. I truly, truly hope that you could continue the classic 2D gameplay and art style from Decisions 1-3 for a Decision 4 or a new sequel. Because I feel that this classic style is another essential soul of the Decision series. If you are short on funding to develop Decision 4, please tell me where I can donate – a website or a channel – and I will donate regularly. I am sure I'm not the only one who loves your games. Many people love them and grew up playing them, but very few of them can still remember your games, because for us Chinese players, the channels to even know about your games are too limited due to internet restrictions. I also hope you could post more development updates or requests for help on Steam. I love your games! Sincerely, A loyal fan from China
